[USER] User is a teacher of a cooking class.  
[USER] User teaches middle school students the basics of healthy and safe cooking.  
[USER] The age of the students is 12-16.  
[USER] User wants to support learners to recall and process accurate foundational information without using quizzes.  
[USER] User believes quizzes enable only short-term recall rather than long-term memorization.  
[USER] User is interested in using instructional strategies proven to increase effective memorization of foundational knowledge.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The first strategy mentioned is known as Undoing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Research shows that learners learn better when the learning experience challenges commonly mistaken foundational ideas and assumptions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The highest impact learning experiences identify and correct foundational misconceptions before memorization occurs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Undoing activities are helpful at the start of the learning process by identifying and correcting gaps in knowledge, misconceptions, and misplaced reasoning.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Undoing activities often ask learners to predict the outcome of a scenario.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] An example of an undoing activity was created regarding Sarah making a healthy sandwich.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] The activity included four options (A, B, C, D) regarding the healthiness of white bread versus whole wheat bread.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Feedback was provided for each potential response, explaining misconceptions and correct conceptions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A resource was suggested: "How to Make Healthy Sandwiches" article on the American Heart Association website.
